description: The third practice project, which moves the P2 catalog API from memory to PostgreSQL or SQL Server with EF Core.
The development-only store (`dotnet user-secrets`) that keeps the connection string out of source control.
The concurrency token the API returns with each product and expects back on `PUT`, so a stale write returns 409.
A single `UPDATE ... WHERE stock >= quantity` issued with `ExecuteUpdateAsync`, whose affected row count decides between 200 and 409.
The number of SQL commands in the EF Core log for one request, the evidence that a report runs as one query.
Removing a product's `HybridCache` entry after a successful update or reservation so the next read is fresh.
